Unde jam subditur : sicut et Christus dilexit nos, id est taliter, utputa pure ac spiritualiter, quamvis non æqualiter, et tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem pacificam et hostiam pro peccato in ara crucis, Deo Patri vel Trinitati, id est ad gloriam ejus, et ut ei pro nobis satisfaceret, in odorem suavitatis, id est in suavem odorem, videlicet in holocaustum acceptissimum atque gratissimum Deo. Maxime enim placuit Deo oblatio Christi ex parte patientis, non ex parte inferentis. Nam ex parte patientis, mors illa erat piissima, et ex summa caritate assumpta ; sed ex parte inferentis, crudelissima erat, sacrilega et displicentissima Deo.
paras.en: Lastly the Apostle continues the moral instruction begun in the preceding chapter, and says: [[5:1|Be ye therefore|Estote ergo]], that is, since God hath forgiven us in Christ, therefore be ye [[5:1|followers of God|imitatores Dei]], that is, conform yourselves to the divine goodness, by sparing those who offend you, doing them good, and loving all, [[5:1|as most dear children|sicut filii carissimi]], my spiritual children or God's adopted children, most dear, that is, greatly beloved, for whom the Father sent and gave His only-begotten, the Son endured death, and the Holy Ghost poured Himself out most abundantly. This is what the Saviour teaches and commands in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:44|Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you|Diligite inimicos vestros, benefacite his qui oderunt vos]], [[Matt 5:45|That you may be the children of your Father who is in heaven, who maketh his sun to rise upon the good, and bad|ut sitis filii Patris vestri qui in cœlis est, qui solem suum oriri facit super bonos et malos]]. Now to be made like the Creator is the highest perfection of the creature, provided the likeness be ordered and not usurped. [[5:2|And walk in love|Et ambulate in dilectione]] of God and of neighbour, living in charity, according to that: [[John 15:12|This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you.|Hoc est præceptum meum, ut diligatis invicem, sicut dilexi vos.]]. Hence it is added: [[5:2|as Christ also hath loved us|sicut et Christus dilexit nos]], that is, in such a manner, namely purely and spiritually, though not equally, [[5:2|and hath delivered himself for us, an oblation|et tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem]] of peace [[5:2|and a sacrifice|et hostiam]] for sin on the altar of the cross, [[5:2|to God|Deo]] the Father, or to the Trinity, that is, to His glory, and to make satisfaction to Him for us, [[5:2|for an odour of sweetness|in odorem suavitatis]], that is, for a sweet odour, namely as a holocaust most acceptable and pleasing to God. For the offering of Christ pleased God supremely on the part of Him who suffered, not on the part of those who inflicted it. For on the part of the sufferer that death was most loving, and undertaken out of the highest charity; but on the part of those who inflicted it, it was most cruel, sacrilegious and most displeasing to God.

paras.t: Fornicatio autem simplex, et omnis immunditia, id est alia quælibet luxuriæ species, aut avaritia, id est inordinatus temporalium appetitus, nec nominetur, id est, non solum non sit, sed nec exprimatur, in vobis, id est a vobis seu inter vos, sicut decet sanctos esse sine talium nominatione ; aut turpitudo, id est indecentia in osculis et amplexibus, aut stultiloquium, sicut est adulatio, aut scurrilitas, id est jocularitas risum concitans, quæ ad rem non pertinet, id est, saluti non proficit. Horum nullum nominetur aut sit in vobis, sed magis gratiarum actio a vobis Domino persolvatur. Per hoc docet Apostolus, quam longe debeant esse magna peccata ab his qui student perfectioni. Hoc enim scitote intelligentes, id est sacram Scripturam sapienter pensantes, quod omnis fornicator, id est cum soluta concumbens, aut immundus, id est aliud aliquod luxuriæ genus exercens, ut est stuprum, incestus, adulterium, aut avarus, quod est idolorum servitus, id est, cujus iniquitas idololatriæ comparatur : eo quod sicut idololatra idola colit magis quam Deum verum, ita avarus potius adhæret argento et auro quam Deo, magisque confidit in eis quam in Domino. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico legitur : Avaro nihil est scelestius ; et nihil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam. Non habet hereditatem, id est beatam possessionem seu paratam felicitatem, in regno Christi et Dei, quod est unum regnum : quia nec modo pertinet ad filios Ecclesiæ militantis per gratiam gratificantem, nec postmodum pertinebit ad cives Ecclesiæ triumphantis per gloriam. Non enim intrabit in illam aliquod coinquinatum, nisi qui scripti fuerint in libro vitæ Agni. Et Isaias ait : Tollatur impius, ne videat gloriam Dei.
paras.en: [[5:3|But fornication|Fornicatio autem]] simple, [[5:3|and all uncleanness|et omnis immunditia]], that is, any other kind of lust, [[5:3|or covetousness|aut avaritia]], that is, inordinate desire of temporal things, [[5:3|let it not so much as be named|nec nominetur]], that is, not only let it not exist, but let it not even be spoken, [[5:3|among you|in vobis]], that is, by you or among you, [[5:3|as becometh saints|sicut decet sanctos]] to be without the naming of such things; [[5:4|Or obscenity|aut turpitudo]], that is, indecency in kisses and embraces, [[5:4|or foolish talking|aut stultiloquium]], such as flattery, [[5:4|or scurrility|aut scurrilitas]], that is, jesting that stirs up laughter, [[5:4|which is to no purpose|quæ ad rem non pertinet]], that is, profits nothing for salvation. Let none of these be named or be among you, [[5:4|but rather giving of thanks|sed magis gratiarum actio]] be paid by you to the Lord. By this the Apostle teaches how far great sins ought to be from those who strive after perfection. [[5:5|For know you this and understand|Hoc enim scitote intelligentes]], that is, weighing Holy Scripture wisely, [[5:5|That no fornicator|quod omnis fornicator]] [literally “every fornicator … hath not”], that is, one who lies with an unmarried woman, [[5:5|or unclean|aut immundus]], that is, practising some other kind of lust, such as seduction, incest, adultery, [[5:5|or covetous person (which is a serving of idols|aut avarus, quod est idolorum servitus]], that is, whose wickedness is likened to idolatry: because as the idolater worships idols rather than the true God, so the covetous man clings to silver and gold rather than to God, and trusts more in them than in the Lord. Wherefore it is read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:9|nothing is more wicked than the covetous man|Avaro nihil est scelestius]]; [[Ecclus 10:10|There is not a more wicked thing than to love money|nihil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam]]. [[5:5|hath inheritance|Non habet hereditatem]], that is, the blessed possession or prepared happiness, [[5:5|in the kingdom of Christ and of God|in regno Christi et Dei]], which is one kingdom: for it neither now belongs to him among the children of the Church militant through sanctifying grace [*gratia gratificans*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], nor will it hereafter belong to him among the citizens of the Church triumphant through glory. For there shall not enter into it anything defiled, but they that are written in the book of life of the Lamb[[Apoc 21:27||]]. And Isaias says: Let the wicked be taken away, that he may not see the glory of God[[Is 26:10||]] [the margin notes this is according to the Septuagint].

paras.t: Nemo vos seducat inanibus verbis, id est coloratis sermonibus, apparentibus argumentis, frivolis promissionibus, providentiam Dei negando, vel impunitatem ex divina misericordia promittendo, seu longam vitam spondendo. Propter hæc enim, id est propter horum inanium verborum prolationem, seductionem seu credulitatem, venit ira, id est ultio, Dei in filios diffidentiæ, id est in homines desperantes de vita futura seu præmiatione divina. Nolite ergo effici participes eorum sic diffidentium, id est, nec affectu, nec opere, neque auxilio conformemini eis. Digni quippe sunt morte, non solum qui faciunt, sed etiam qui consentiunt. Nam et qui tetigerit picem, inquinabitur ab ea.
paras.en: [[5:6|Let no man deceive you with vain words|Nemo vos seducat inanibus verbis]], that is, with specious speeches, plausible arguments, frivolous promises, denying the providence of God, or promising impunity from the divine mercy, or pledging a long life. [[5:6|For because of these things|Propter hæc enim]], that is, because of the uttering of these vain words, the seduction or the credulity, [[5:6|cometh the anger|venit ira]], that is, the vengeance, [[5:6|of God upon the children of unbelief|Dei in filios diffidentiæ]], that is, upon men despairing of the life to come or of the divine reward. [[5:7|Be ye not therefore partakers with them|Nolite ergo effici participes eorum]] who so distrust, that is, conform not yourselves to them in affection, nor in deed, nor by help. For they are worthy of death, not only they that do them, but they also that consent[[Rom 1:32||]]. For [[Ecclus 13:1|He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled with it|qui tetigerit picem, inquinabitur ab ea]].

paras.t: Eratis enim aliquando, dum mundo et concupiscentiis inhæsistis, tenebræ, id est, tanta vitiorum caligine, cordis cæcitate, et ignorantiæ tenebris involuti, ut non solum tenebrosi, sed etiam tenebræ fuisse dicamini ; nunc autem, quando ad Deum conversi estis, facti estis lux, id est spiritualiter illuminati, in Domino, id est in veritate et gratia Dei. Idcirco, Ut filii lucis ambulate, id est, pure, honeste ac religiose conversemini, sicut ad filios lucis pertinet, id est ad filios Dei, qui est lux æterna et increata, juxta illud Joannis : Erat lux vera. Vel per lucem, intelligitur splendor seu claritas gratiæ, cujus filii sunt omnes qui gratiam habent. Unde ait Salvator : Dum lucem habetis, credite in lucem, ut filii lucis sitis. Merito autem sic debetis ambulare : Fructus enim lucis, id est operatio gratiæ, vel opus placitum luci æternæ, est vivere in omni bonitate, id est interna virtute ac pietate, quoad se ipsum, et justitia, id est in justa actione, quantum ad proximum, et veritate, quantum ad Deum, ei veraciter ministrando ; probantes, id est prudenter investigantes, vel rationabiliter discernentes, quid sit beneplacitum Deo, ut illud semper agatis, et quæ displicent Deo vitetis. Unde apud Jeremiam ait Dominus : Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris.
paras.en: [[5:8|For you were heretofore|Eratis enim aliquando]], while you clung to the world and its lusts, [[5:8|darkness|tenebræ]], that is, wrapped in such a fog of vices, blindness of heart and darkness of ignorance, that you may be said to have been not only darksome but darkness itself; [[5:8|but now|nunc autem]], since you have been converted to God, you are made [[5:8|light|lux]], that is, spiritually enlightened, [[5:8|in the Lord|in Domino]], that is, in the truth and grace of God. Therefore, [[5:8|Walk then as children of the light|Ut filii lucis ambulate]], that is, live purely, honestly and devoutly, as befits the children of light, that is, the children of God, who is the eternal and uncreated light, according to that of John: [[John 1:9|That was the true light|Erat lux vera]]. Or by light is understood the splendour or brightness of grace, whose children are all who have grace. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 12:36|Whilst you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be the children of light|Dum lucem habetis, credite in lucem, ut filii lucis sitis]]. And rightly ought you so to walk: [[5:9|For the fruit of the light|Fructus enim lucis]], that is, the working of grace, or the work pleasing to the eternal light, [[5:9|is|est]] to live [[5:9|in all goodness|in omni bonitate]], that is, in inward virtue and devotion, as regards oneself, [[5:9|and justice|et justitia]], that is, in just action, as regards one's neighbour, [[5:9|and truth|et veritate]], as regards God, serving Him truly; [[5:10|Proving|probantes]], that is, prudently searching out, or reasonably discerning, [[5:10|what is well pleasing to God|quid sit beneplacitum Deo]], that you may always do it, and avoid what displeases God. Hence the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 15:19|If thou wilt be converted, I will convert thee, and thou shalt stand before my face; and thou wilt separate the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth|Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris]].

paras.t: Et nolite communicare, consentiendo vel cooperando, operibus infructuosis, id est vacuis a fructu spirituali, tenebrarum, id est malorum habituum seu hominum mentibus obscuratorum ; magis autem redarguite, id est, iterum atque iterum corripite, si sit spes de emendatione, et maxime, si ad vestram pertineant curam qui peccant. Omnes tamen ad correctionem fraternam jure caritatis aliquo modo tenentur. His ergo duobus modis, secundum Augustinum, non te maculat malus : si non consentis, et si redarguis. Quoniam enim parum est non consentire, jungit Apostolus quod majus est, Magis autem redarguite. Propter quod ait Salvator : Si peccaverit in te frater tuus, id est te sciente, vade et corripe eum inter te et ipsum solum, etc.
paras.en: [[5:11|And have no fellowship with|Et nolite communicare]], by consenting or cooperating, [[5:11|the unfruitful works|operibus infructuosis]], that is, empty of spiritual fruit, [[5:11|of darkness|tenebrarum]], that is, of evil habits or of men darkened in mind; [[5:11|but rather reprove them|magis autem redarguite]], that is, rebuke them again and again, if there be hope of amendment, and especially if those who sin belong to your charge. Yet all are in some way bound to fraternal correction by the law of charity. In these two ways, then, according to Augustine, the wicked man does not stain thee: if thou consent not, and if thou reprove. For since it is little not to consent, the Apostle adds what is greater: But rather reprove them. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Matt 18:15|But if thy brother shall offend against thee, go, and rebuke him between thee and him alone|Si peccaverit in te frater tuus, id est te sciente, vade et corripe eum inter te et ipsum solum]], that is, with thy knowledge, etc.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit, quare non debeamus communicare operibus impiorum. Quæ enim in occulto, id est in locis absconditis, fiunt ab ipsis prædictis excæcatis hominibus, humanum potius quam divinum conspectum timentibus, turpe est et dicere : quanto magis facere? Omnia autem quæ arguuntur, id est opera quæ reprehenduntur, a lumine manifestantur, id est, per veram locutionem, splendidamque doctrinam increpantis, innotescunt esse digna reprobatione, nec ultra valent latere, quemadmodum ad Timotheum ipse ait : Insipientia illorum omnibus manifesta erit. Omne enim quod manifestatur hoc modo, per increpationem vel humilem peccantis confessionem, lumen est, id est clarum, certum ac notum ; vel, Lumen est, id est, spirituali luce perfunditur, dum in publicum ducitur. His consonat verbum Christi : Omnis qui male agit, odit lucem, et non venit ad lucem, ut non arguantur opera ejus ; qui autem facit veritatem, venit ad lucem, ut manifestentur opera ejus, quia in Deo sunt facta.
paras.en: Next he shows why we ought not to have fellowship with the works of the ungodly. [[5:12|For the things that are done by them in secret|Quæ enim in occulto]], that is, in hidden places, [[5:12|that are done by them|fiunt ab ipsis]], by the aforesaid blinded men, who fear the sight of men rather than of God, [[5:12|it is a shame even to speak of|turpe est et dicere]]: how much more to do them? [[5:13|But all things that are reproved|Omnia autem quæ arguuntur]], that is, the works that are rebuked, [[5:13|are made manifest by the light|a lumine manifestantur]], that is, through the true speech and shining doctrine of the one who rebukes, they are made known to be worthy of condemnation, and can no longer lie hid, as he himself says to Timothy: [[2 Tim 3:9|their folly shall be manifest to all|Insipientia illorum omnibus manifesta erit]]. [[5:13|for all that is made manifest|Omne enim quod manifestatur]] in this way, by rebuke or by the humble confession of the sinner, [[5:13|is light|lumen est]], that is, clear, certain and known; or, Is light, that is, is flooded with spiritual light when it is brought into the open. With this agrees the word of Christ: [[John 3:20|For every one that doth evil hateth the light and cometh not to the light, that his works may not be reproved|Omnis qui male agit, odit lucem, et non venit ad lucem, ut non arguantur opera ejus]]; [[John 3:21|But he that doth truth cometh to the light, that his works may be made manifest: because they are done in God|qui autem facit veritatem, venit ad lucem, ut manifestentur opera ejus, quia in Deo sunt facta]].

paras.t: Propter quod, videlicet quoniam lumen est quod manifestatur, dicit Spiritus Sanctus per me : Surge a vitiis per pœnitentiam, qui dormis, id est, in ignavia tua quiescis, et exsurge per opera pœnitentialia a mortuis, id est de societate impœnitentium spiritualiter mortuorum, et illuminabit te, id est, radium sapientiæ et lumen discretionis tribuet tibi, Christus : juxta illud Isaiæ : Requiem dabit tibi Dominus semper, et implebit splendoribus animam tuam, si glorificaveris Dominum, dum non facis vias tuas. Unde Michæas ait : Quum sedero in tenebris, Dominus lux mea est ; et deducet me Dominus in lucem, et videbo justitiam ejus.
paras.en: [[5:14|Wherefore|Propter quod]], namely because what is made manifest is light, [[5:14|he saith|dicit]], the Holy Ghost through me: [[5:14|Rise|Surge]] from vices by penance, [[5:14|thou that sleepest|qui dormis]], that is, who restest in thy sloth, [[5:14|and arise|et exsurge]] by works of penance [[5:14|from the dead|a mortuis]], that is, from the company of the impenitent who are spiritually dead, [[5:14|and Christ shall enlighten thee|et illuminabit te Christus]], that is, Christ shall give thee a ray of wisdom and the light of discernment: according to that of Isaias: The Lord will give thee rest continually, and will fill thy soul with brightness[[Is 58:11||]], if thou glorify the Lord while thou dost not thine own ways[[Is 58:13||]] [the margin seems to read Is. xxxviii, 11, 13; the words are from Is 58:11, 13]. Hence Micheas says: [[Mich 7:8|when I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light|Quum sedero in tenebris, Dominus lux mea est]]; [[Mich 7:9|he will bring me forth into the light, I shall behold his justice|deducet me Dominus in lucem, et videbo justitiam ejus]] [the margin gives Mich. viii; the passage is Mich 7:8–9].

paras.t: Videte itaque, fratres, id est, oculo intellectuali pensate, quomodo caute ambuletis, id est, vigilanter et custodite vivatis, occasiones peccati vitando, atque in arcta via quæ ducit ad vitam, cum omni circumspectione progrediendo, ut impleatis quod a Sapiente dicitur : Omni custodia custodi cor tuum ; et quod rursus idem ait, In timore Domini esto tota die, et habebis spem in novissimo ; non quasi insipientes, id est sola temporalia atque præsentia bona seu mala considerantes, sed ut sapientes in cognitione divinorum, id est discreti ac providi, cœlestibus bonis semper intenti ; redimentes, id est ab infructuosis occupationibus expedientes, tempus vitæ præsentis, id est certas horas ad vacandum Deo aptantes. Vel, Redimentes tempus, id est tempora quæ infructuose expendistis, reparantes per fructuosissimam occupationem temporis præsentis atque restantis : quatenus priores negligentias et impietates recompensetis per ardentissimam conversationem temporis nondum elapsi quo estis victuri, ne inter impios numeremini, de quibus canit Psalmographus : Viri sanguinum et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos. Quoniam dies mali sunt, id est adversitatibus, periculis atque malitiis pleni. Non quod dies in se mali sint, sed quia hæc mala insunt hominibus in diebus sæculi hujus viventibus. Scriptura enim tempori ea adscribit quæ fiunt in tempore, quemadmodum primo Machabæorum inducitur : Videns Jonathas quia tempus eum juvat. Hinc enim Salvator : Sufficit, inquit, diei malitia sua. Et in Genesi Jacob asseruit : Dies peregrinationis meæ parvi et mali.
paras.en: [[5:15|See therefore, brethren|Videte itaque, fratres]], that is, weigh with the eye of the understanding, [[5:15|how you walk circumspectly|quomodo caute ambuletis]], that is, live watchfully and guardedly, avoiding occasions of sin, and advancing with all circumspection in the narrow way that leadeth to life[[Matt 7:14||]] [the margin reads Matth. xv, 14; the narrow way is Matt 7:14], that you may fulfil what is said by the Wise Man: [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness keep thy heart|Omni custodia custodi cor tuum]] [the margin reads Prov. xxi, 24; the words are Prov 4:23]; and what he says again: [[Prov 23:17|be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long|In timore Domini esto tota die]]; [[Prov 23:18|thou shalt have hope in the latter|habebis spem in novissimo]]; [[5:15|not as unwise|non quasi insipientes]], that is, considering only temporal and present goods or evils, [[5:16|But as wise|sed ut sapientes]] in the knowledge of divine things, that is, discerning and provident, ever intent on heavenly goods; [[5:16|redeeming|redimentes]], that is, freeing from unfruitful occupations, [[5:16|the time|tempus]] of the present life, that is, setting aside fixed hours for attending to God. Or, Redeeming the time, that is, making good the times you spent unfruitfully by a most fruitful use of the present and remaining time: so that you may make up for former negligences and impieties by a most fervent life in the time not yet elapsed that you have yet to live, lest you be numbered among the ungodly, of whom the Psalmist sings: [[Ps 54:24|Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days|Viri sanguinum et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos]]. [[5:16|because the days are evil|Quoniam dies mali sunt]], that is, full of adversities, dangers and wickednesses. Not that the days are evil in themselves, but because these evils are in men living in the days of this world. For Scripture ascribes to time the things that are done in time, as is said in the first of Machabees: Jonathas saw that the time served him[[1 Mach 12:1||]]. Hence too the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:34|Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof|Sufficit, inquit, diei malitia sua]]. And in Genesis Jacob declared: [[Gen 47:9|The days of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years, few, and evil|Dies peregrinationis meæ parvi et mali]].

paras.t: Propterea nolite fieri imprudentes, sola sensibilia et temporalia ponderando ; sed intelligentes quæ sit voluntas Dei, id est, hoc diligentissime inquiratis, quid placeat Deo, ut illud semper agatis.
paras.en: [[5:17|Wherefore, become not unwise|Propterea nolite fieri imprudentes]], by weighing only things of sense and of time; [[5:17|but understanding what is the will of God|sed intelligentes quæ sit voluntas Dei]], that is, inquire most diligently into this, what pleases God, that you may always do it.

paras.t: Et nolite inebriari vino, in quo est luxuria causaliter, quia calorem auget atque libidinem concitat. Venter enim vino æstuans, cito spumat in libidinem, juxta Hieronymum. Unde Sapiens dicit : Luxuriosa res vinum, et tumultuosa ebrietas ; qui his delectatur, non erit sapiens. Rursusque Scriptura : Quam sufficiens est homini erudito vinum exiguum! Sed implemini Spiritu Sancto, id est, ita vivatis, et corda vestra sic occupetis, ut in gratia Spiritus Sancti proficiatis quotidie : Deus enim unicuique influit, secundum quod se disponit aut capax efficitur. Loquentes vobismetipsis, id est mutuo exhortantes vos ipsos, in psalmis ad bene operandum hortantibus, et hymnis ad Dei laudem spectantibus, et canticis spiritualibus quæ de gaudiis futuris commemorant, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris, id est silenter in anima ; vel, In cordibus vestris, id est cum cordiali intentione et ex mentali affectu ; Domino Deo altissimo, quem decet hymnus, laus, honor et gloria. Gratias agentes semper, id est qualibet hora convenienti ac debita, pro omnibus beneficiis Dei, vel pro omnibus hominibus beneficia divina sortitis, omnium saluti congratulando, in nomine nominato Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est in ipso Christo, videlicet ad laudem et gloriam ejus, vel certe per eum, Deo et Patri, id est Patri æterno, qui est Deus ratione creationis, paterque Christi naturalis, et pater noster adoptivus. Subjecti invicem ex debito obedientiæ, vel ex condecentia humilitatis et caritatis, in timore Dei casto ac filiali. Prælati enim per humilitatem et caritatem subdunt se inferioribus ; subditi vero ex debito obedientiæ subjiciuntur prælatis. Ceteri omnes communiter se invicem honorare præferreque habent, juxta illud quod alibi dictum est : Honore invicem prævenientes. Propter quod Christus testatur : Qui major est vestrum, sit vester minister ; et iterum legitur, Quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus.
paras.en: [[5:18|And be not drunk with wine, wherein is luxury|Et nolite inebriari vino, in quo est luxuria]], as its cause, because it increases heat and stirs up lust. For the belly seething with wine soon foams over into lust, according to Jerome. Hence the Wise Man says: [[Prov 20:1|Wine is a luxurious thing, and drunkenness riotous: whosoever is delighted therewith, shall not be wise|Luxuriosa res vinum, et tumultuosa ebrietas ; qui his delectatur, non erit sapiens]]. And again Scripture: [[Ecclus 31:22|How sufficient is a little wine for a man well taught|Quam sufficiens est homini erudito vinum exiguum]]. [[5:18|but be ye filled with the Holy Spirit|Sed implemini Spiritu Sancto]], that is, so live and so occupy your hearts that you may advance daily in the grace of the Holy Ghost: for God flows into each one according as he disposes himself or is made capable. [[5:19|Speaking to yourselves|Loquentes vobismetipsis]], that is, exhorting one another, [[5:19|in psalms|in psalmis]] that exhort to good works, [[5:19|and hymns|et hymnis]] that look to the praise of God, [[5:19|and spiritual canticles|et canticis spiritualibus]] that recall the joys to come, [[5:19|singing and making melody in your hearts|cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris]], that is, silently in the soul; or, In your hearts, that is, with heartfelt intention and from the affection of the mind; [[5:19|to the Lord|Domino]] God most high, to whom a hymn becometh[[Ps 64:2||]], praise, honour and glory. [[5:20|Giving thanks always|Gratias agentes semper]], that is, at every fitting and due hour, [[5:20|for all things|pro omnibus]], for all God's benefits, or for all men who have received divine benefits, rejoicing in the salvation of all, [[5:20|in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ|in nomine nominato Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], the name that is named, that is, in Christ Himself, namely to His praise and glory, or else through Him, [[5:20|to God and the Father|Deo et Patri]], that is, to the eternal Father, who is God by reason of creation, and the natural Father of Christ, and our adoptive Father. [[5:21|Being subject one to another|Subjecti invicem]] from the duty of obedience, or from the fittingness of humility and charity, [[5:21|in the fear of|in timore]] God [Denis's text reads *Dei*, the Vulgate *Christi*], chaste and filial. For prelates subject themselves to their inferiors through humility and charity, while subjects are subject to prelates from the duty of obedience. All others in common ought to honour and prefer one another, according to what is said elsewhere: [[Rom 12:10|with honour preventing one another|Honore invicem prævenientes]]. Wherefore Christ testifies: [[Matt 20:26|whosoever is the greater among you, let him be your minister|Qui major est vestrum, sit vester minister]] [cf. Matt 23:11[[Matt 23:11||]]]; and again it is read: [[Ecclus 3:20|The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things|Quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus]].

paras.t: Præterea generalibus exhortationibus positis, descendit Apostolus ad particulares personas, dicendo : Mulieres viris suis subditæ sint in licitis et honestis, sicut domino, id est, sicut domino subditur servus ; quoniam vir caput, id est superior, est mulieris, id est perfectior atque discretior ea communiter. Et Dominus prætulit virum feminæ, dicens ad eam : Sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui. Sicut et Christus caput, id est rector ac princeps, est Ecclesiæ : ipse Christus exsistens salvator corporis ejus, id est Ecclesiæ, quæ est mysticum corpus Christi. Sed sicut Ecclesia, id est fidelium sancta collectio, subjecta est Christo fide et opere, ita et mulieres viris suis in omnibus bonis sint subditæ. Sciendum tamen, quod subjectio mulieris sub viro, non est in omnibus similis subjectioni ancillæ aut servi, quum ipsa sit socia viri, et una caro cum eo, facta non de capite aut pedibus, sed de latere viri, quasi similis ei, et juxta latus ejus ponenda.
paras.en: Further, the general exhortations having been set down, the Apostle comes down to particular persons, saying: [[5:22|Let women be subject to their husbands|Mulieres viris suis subditæ sint]][[Col 3:18||]] in things lawful and honest, [[5:22|as to the Lord|sicut domino]], that is, as a servant is subject to his lord; [[5:23|Because the husband is the head|quoniam vir caput]], that is, the superior, [[5:23|of the wife|est mulieris]][[1 Cor 11:3||]], that is, commonly more perfect and more discerning than she. And the Lord set the man over the woman, saying to her: [[Gen 3:16|thou shalt be under thy husband's power, and he shall have dominion over thee|Sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui]]. [[5:23|as Christ is the head|Sicut et Christus caput]], that is, ruler and prince, [[5:23|of the church. He|est Ecclesiæ : ipse]], Christ, being [[5:23|the saviour of his body|salvator corporis ejus]], that is, of the Church, which is the mystical body of Christ. [[5:24|Therefore as the church|Sed sicut Ecclesia]], that is, the holy gathering of the faithful, [[5:24|is subject to Christ|subjecta est Christo]] in faith and deed, [[5:24|so also let the wives be to their husbands in all things|ita et mulieres viris suis in omnibus]] good be subject. Yet it must be known that the subjection of the wife to the husband is not in all respects like the subjection of a handmaid or servant, since she is the companion of the man and one flesh with him[[Matt 19:5||]], made not from his head or feet but from his side[[Gen 2:21||]], as like to him and to be placed at his side.

paras.t: Viri, diligite uxores vestras, non carnali et fœdo, sed ordinato ac spirituali amore, sicut et Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et se ipsum tradidit in mortem pro ea, id est pro ejus salute, ut illam sanctificaret, id est, virtutibus adornaret, mundans eam primo, id est a vitiis purgans, lavacro aquæ, id est intinctione seu lotione in aqua Baptismatis : lavacro, inquam, facto in verbo vitæ, id est sub debita forma verborum quibus hoc sacramentum ex Christi institutione perficitur. Accedit quippe verbum ad elementum, et fit sacramentum : in quo verbum est formale ac principale, elementum vero est materiale. Ut exhiberet, id est, repræsentaret vel faceret, ipse Christus sponsus cœlestis, sibi, id est ad suum honorem, secundum quod Deus est, in præsenti sæculo inchoative, in futuro autem completive, gloriosam Ecclesiam, id est claritate scientiæ atque virtutum splendoribus refulgentem, non habentem maculam, id est peccatum mortale apertum, aut rugam, id est peccatum mortale occultum, sed mundam ac simplicem, aut aliquid hujusmodi criminale habentem ; sed ut sit sancta in interioribus, et immaculata in exterioribus. Ita et viri debent diligere uxores suas ut corpora sua, quia sunt una caro. Si autem sumatur corpus pro parte hominis materiali, sic viri magis tenentur diligere uxores suas quam corpora propria ; si vero sumatur corpus pro toto composito, minus diligendæ sunt uxores. Ideo similitudo est quantum ad aliquid, non absolute in omnibus.
paras.en: [[5:25|Husbands, love your wives|Viri, diligite uxores vestras]][[Col 3:19||]], not with a carnal and foul love but with an ordered and spiritual one, [[5:25|as Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up|sicut et Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et se ipsum tradidit]] to death [[5:25|for it|pro ea]], that is, for its salvation, [[5:26|That he might sanctify it|ut illam sanctificaret]], that is, adorn it with virtues, [[5:26|cleansing it|mundans eam]] first, that is, purging it of vices, [[5:26|by the laver of water|lavacro aquæ]], that is, by dipping or washing in the water of Baptism: a laver, I say, made [[5:26|in the word of life|in verbo vitæ]], that is, under the due form of words by which this sacrament is accomplished by Christ's institution. For the word is joined to the element, and it becomes a sacrament: in which the word is formal and principal, and the element material [that is, in scholastic terms, the words are the “form” and the water the “matter” of the sacrament]. [[5:27|That he might present|Ut exhiberet]], that is, show forth or make, [[5:27|it to himself|ipse sibi]] [Denis: *ipse*, Christ the heavenly Bridegroom; *sibi*, that is, to His own honour], according as He is God, in the present world in its beginning, in the world to come in its completion, [[5:27|a glorious church|gloriosam Ecclesiam]], that is, shining with the brightness of knowledge and the splendours of virtues, [[5:27|not having spot|non habentem maculam]], that is, open mortal sin, [[5:27|or wrinkle|aut rugam]], that is, hidden mortal sin, but clean and simple, [[5:27|or any such thing|aut aliquid hujusmodi]] criminal; [[5:27|but that it should be holy|sed ut sit sancta]] within, [[5:27|and without blemish|et immaculata]] without. [[5:28|So also ought men to love their wives as their own bodies|Ita et viri debent diligere uxores suas ut corpora sua]], since they are one flesh[[Gen 2:24||]]. But if body is taken for the material part of man, then husbands are bound to love their wives more than their own bodies; but if body is taken for the whole composite, wives are to be loved less. So the likeness holds in some respect, not absolutely in all.

paras.t: Porro de hac Christi gloriosa et illibata Ecclesia scriptum est in Apocalypsi : Vidi sanctam civitatem Jerusalem novam, descendentem de cœlo, a Deo paratam quasi sponsam ornatam viro suo ; et rursus : Quia venerunt nuptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparavit se. Itemque : Signum magnum apparuit in cœlo : Mulier amicta sole, et luna sub pedibus ejus, et in capite ejus corona stellarum duodecim. De qua etiam intelligendum est illud Isaiæ : Surge, illuminare, Jerusalem, quia venit lumen tuum, et gloria Domini super te orta est.
paras.en: Moreover of this glorious and spotless Church of Christ it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:2|I, John, saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband|Vidi sanctam civitatem Jerusalem novam, descendentem de cœlo, a Deo paratam quasi sponsam ornatam viro suo]]; and again: [[Apoc 19:7|For the marriage of the Lamb is come: and his wife hath prepared herself|Quia venerunt nuptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparavit se]]. And likewise: [[Apoc 12:1|And a great sign appeared in heaven: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.|Et signum magnum apparuit in cælo: mulier amicta sole, et luna sub pedibus ejus, et in capite ejus corona stellarum duodecim:]]. Of her too is to be understood that of Isaias: [[Is 60:1|Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem: for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.|Surge, illuminare, Jerusalem, quia venit lumen tuum, et gloria Domini super te orta est.]].

paras.t: Qui suam uxorem diligit, se ipsum diligit : tanta est unitas utriusque. Sunt namque duo in carne una. Merito itaque debet homo uxorem suam diligere : Nemo enim, id est nullus rationabiliter et humane se habens, unquam carnem suam odio habuit. Vel simpliciter : Nemo unquam carnem suam odio habuit, quia vel dilectione naturali, vel amore carnali, vel caritate infusa ad eam afficitur. Nam et qui se ipsos occidunt, carnem suam amasse probantur : quam ideo perimunt, ut brevi tormento longa evadant præsentis vitæ supplicia. Sed nutrit victu, et fovet eam vestitu, sicut et Christus Ecclesiam nutrit Sacramento altaris, et fovet eam vestimento salutis :
paras.en: [[5:28|He that loveth his wife loveth himself|Qui suam uxorem diligit, se ipsum diligit]]: so great is the unity of both. For they are two in one flesh[[Gen 2:24||]]. Rightly therefore ought a man to love his wife: [[5:29|For no man|Nemo enim]], that is, no one behaving reasonably and humanely, [[5:29|ever hated his own flesh|unquam carnem suam odio habuit]]. Or simply: No man ever hated his own flesh, because he is drawn to it either by natural love, or by carnal love, or by infused charity. For even those who kill themselves are shown to have loved their flesh: they destroy it so that by a brief torment they may escape the long torments of the present life. [[5:29|but nourisheth|Sed nutrit]] it with food, [[5:29|and cherisheth it|et fovet eam]] with clothing, [[5:29|as also Christ doth the church|sicut et Christus Ecclesiam]], nourishing it with the Sacrament of the altar, and cherishing it with the garment of salvation:

paras.t: quia membra sumus nos Christiani, corporis ejus, id est Ecclesiæ, quæ est mysticum corpus Christi. Sumus itaque membra de carne ejus et de ossibus ejus, id est ejusdem naturæ existentes cum Christo homine. Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quia fidelium qui a Christo instituti sunt, quidam, puta infirmi, dicuntur de carne Christi, quæ ante passionem erat infirma, quoniam indigent a fortibus sustentari, quemadmodum caro sustentatur ab ossibus. Alii, scilicet fortes atque perfecti, dicuntur de ossibus Christi, propter constantiam et dominicæ passionis ac patientiæ imitationem. Propter hoc, id est ad designandum dilectionem ac unitatem Christi atque Ecclesiæ, scriptum est in Genesi, relinquet homo, id est maritus, patrem suum et matrem suam, id est carnales parentes, quantum ad cohabitationem localem, et adhærebit uxori suæ, habitando, convescendo et dormiendo cum ea ; et erunt duo supposita, scilicet maritus et conjux, in carne una, id est in uno carnali commercio per seminis propagationem. Vel dicuntur duo in carne una, quoniam nullus eorum propriæ carnis habet potestatem, et propter communionem præcipuam una caro reputantur. Unde dicit Salvator : Itaque jam non sunt duo, sed una caro. Deinde ponit Apostolus mysticum sen-
paras.en: [[5:30|Because we are members|quia membra sumus]], we Christians, [[5:30|of him, body|corporis ejus]] [literally “of his body”], that is, of the Church, which is the mystical body of Christ[[Col 1:24||]]. We are therefore members [[5:30|of his flesh and of his bones|de carne ejus et de ossibus ejus]], that is, being of the same nature as Christ the man. Or it is said for this reason: that of the faithful instructed by Christ, some, namely the weak, are said to be of the flesh of Christ, which before the passion was weak, because they need to be supported by the strong, as flesh is supported by the bones. Others, namely the strong and perfect, are said to be of the bones of Christ, because of their constancy and their imitation of the Lord's passion and patience. [[5:31|For this cause|Propter hoc]], that is, to signify the love and unity of Christ and the Church, it is written in Genesis[[Gen 2:24||]][[Matt 19:5||]]: [[5:31|shall a man|relinquet homo]], that is, the husband, [[5:31|leave his father and mother|patrem suum et matrem suam]], that is, his carnal parents, as regards dwelling in one place, [[5:31|and shall cleave to his wife|et adhærebit uxori suæ]], dwelling, eating and sleeping with her; [[5:31|And they shall be two|et erunt duo]] persons [*supposita*, individual subjects], namely husband and wife, [[5:31|in one flesh|in carne una]], that is, in one carnal union for the propagation of offspring. Or they are said to be two in one flesh because neither of them has power over his own flesh[[1 Cor 7:4||]], and because of their special communion they are reckoned one flesh. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 19:6|Therefore now they are not two, but one flesh|Itaque jam non sunt duo, sed una caro]]. Next the Apostle sets down the mystical sense

paras.t: sum Scripturæ de matrimonio allegatæ. Sacramentum hoc, id est sacrum signum istud in conjugio pronuntiatum, magnum est, id est magnæ rei significativum. Ego autem dico, id est, signum istud expono, impletumque assero, in Christo et in Ecclesia, id est in spirituali desponsatione inter Christum et Ecclesiam facta, quando videlicet Verbum caro factum est, et nostram naturam assumens, ostendit quantum dilexerit nos, cum quibus idem fieri voluit. Matrimonium ergo seu conjugium, magnum est sacramentum, propter significantiam conjunctionis Christi et Ecclesiæ : in qua etiam Christus quodammodo Patrem reliquisse videtur, non simpliciter, quum æternaliter sit in sinu, imo in corde Patris, sed secundum apparentiam quamdam ratione incarnationis. Sic enim de novo apparuit mundo, ad conjungendum sibi Ecclesiam tanquam sponsam. Propter quod ait : Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum. Et Psalmista : Ipse, inquit, tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo ; a summo cœlo egressio ejus. Matrem quoque suam, id est Synagogam, Christus reliquit, et adhæsit uxori suæ, id est gentilitati conversæ, quam ipse spiritualiter visitat et fecundat. Verumtamen, id est, quamvis prædicta de conjugio mystice intelligantur de Christo, nihilo minus et vos singuli, id est unusquisque vestrum conjugem habens, suam uxorem sicut se ipsum diligat. Uxor autem timeat virum suum, id est, in reverentia habeat eum, et casto timore formidet, ne eum offendat.
paras.en: of the Scripture cited about marriage. [[5:32|This is a great sacrament|Sacramentum hoc magnum est]]: this, that is, this sacred sign declared in marriage, is great, that is, signifies a great thing. [[5:32|but I speak|Ego autem dico]], that is, I expound this sign and declare it fulfilled, [[5:32|in Christ and in the church|in Christo et in Ecclesia]], that is, in the spiritual espousal made between Christ and the Church, namely when the Word was made flesh[[John 1:14||]], and taking our nature showed how much He loved us, with whom He willed to become one. Matrimony, then, or wedlock, is a great sacrament, because it signifies the union of Christ and the Church: in which Christ too seems in a manner to have left His Father, not simply, since He is eternally in the bosom, nay in the heart, of the Father, but according to a certain appearance by reason of the incarnation. For thus He appeared anew to the world, to join the Church to Himself as a bride. Wherefore He says: [[John 16:28|I came forth from the Father and am come into the world|Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 18:6|as a bridegroom coming out of his bridechamber|tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo]]; [[Ps 18:7|His going out is from the end of heaven|a summo cœlo egressio ejus]]. His mother also, that is, the Synagogue, Christ left, and cleaved to His wife, that is, the converted Gentiles, whom He spiritually visits and makes fruitful. [[5:33|Nevertheless|Verumtamen]], that is, although what has been said of marriage is understood mystically of Christ, none the less [[5:33|let every one of you|et vos singuli, id est unusquisque]], that is, each of you who has a wife, [[5:33|love for his wife as himself|uxorem suam sicut se ipsum diligat]]. [[5:33|And let the wife fear her husband|Uxor autem timeat virum suum]], that is, hold him in reverence, and dread with a chaste fear lest she offend him.
